pr_title: Add `codespaces-keypair` flag to `gh cs ssh` command to always use codespaces generated keypair
pr_body:
<!--
  Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!
  To reference an open issue, please write this in your description: `Fixes #NUMBER`
-->

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/6636

The `gh cli ssh` command is capable of generating its own keypair for SSH. The documentation for the SSH command says that the ssh command will "By default... create a public/private ssh key pair to authenticate with the codespace inside the ~/.ssh directory." That's not entirely true, however.

The key precedence is: 

1. Key which is specified by `-i`
1. Automatic key, if it already exists
1. First valid keypair in ssh config (according to ssh `-G`)
1. Automatic key, newly created

The "First valid keypair step" runs the ssh command with `-G` (like it says) and then checks for identity files. The identity files that I saw when debugging were: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/80130182/202241189-2a48dff1-d191-4eb3-a348-c56424f26d0d.png)

When trying to use other SSH libraries to SSH to the codespace, we have seen failures related to not having the generated keypair (like the library detecting a different invalid keypair). This PR adds a flag to the `gh cs ssh` command that allows the user to guarantee the use of the codespace generated keypair so users can specify the codespaces generated keys for any SSH flow they may have.
pr_comments: Hi! Thanks for the pull request. Please ensure that this change is linked to an issue by mentioning an issue number in the description of the pull request. If this pull request would close the issue, please put the word 'Fixes' before the issue number somewhere in the pull request body. If this is a tiny change like fixing a typo, feel free to ignore this message.

>When trying to use other SSH libraries to SSH to the codespace, we have seen failures related to not having the generated keypair (like the library detecting a different invalid keypair)

Can you elaborate on this a little bit? What other libraries? And what are the failures that you mention?

I'm also wondering if this is better as a one-time command rather than a parameter that needs to be added to each `cs ssh` instance. What I mean is, the user could one-time run `gh cs ssh --create-keys` and that would create the automatic keys and exit. Thus all future checks would use the keys without the need for the override flag.

I could see a one-time command making sense, maybe in addition to these changes even. One of my concerns about the separate command is that it requires slightly more knowledge about the implementation details of how the key precedence is determined. Where as the flag in the ssh command is declarative--we know that we're going to use the `codespace.auto` key pair. 

> Thus all future checks would use the keys without the need for the override flag.

Once the `codespaces.auto` keys are created they'll always be used over the detected keys in the ssh directory, so it wouldn't need to be included in the `2..n` call, it would just guarantee that keys are there at the end of the call. 

I also avoided using the `create` or `generate` verbiage because it won't nuke the keys if they exist, it will only create them if they don't (which I think is the right behavior here). 

In any case, I think that the description of the SSH command should be updated to reflect that the generation isn't entirely by default depending on the existing keys in your ssh directory.

FWIW I built this branch just to use this option to generate a `codespaces.auto` file, because I kept getting errors like this when trying to ssh to my codespaces

```
vscode@localhost: Permission denied (publickey,password).
```

This is after dumping the ssh config like it shows in the help docs for `gh cs ssh --help` (cause then I can add some useful config under a `Host github-codespaces` entry in my ssh config)

```
EXAMPLES
  $ gh codespace ssh

  $ gh codespace ssh --config > ~/.ssh/codespaces
  $ printf 'Match all\nInclude ~/.ssh/codespaces\n' >> ~/.ssh/config
```

However, this hardcodes a `-i` flag

```
% grep codespaces.auto ~/.ssh/codespaces
        ProxyCommand /opt/homebrew/bin/gh cs ssh -c mmrobins-mycodespacename --stdio -- -i /Users/mmrobins/.ssh/codespaces.auto
        IdentityFile /Users/mmrobins/.ssh/codespaces.auto
```

And that `codespaces.auto` file never exists by default, which is confusing.  I could just modify the `.ssh/codespaces` file, but it'd be nice if either

* that `/.ssh/codespaces.auto` always got generated, manually or automatically
* the `gh codespace ssh --config` command was smart enough to know what to put in config for existing identity files

issue_context.title: Add flag to `gh cs ssh` that forces it to use `codespaces.auto` keys
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

The CLI will automatically generate a keypair to use for ssh'ing to a codespace in most cases. However, if the generated keys don't exist and the CLI finds a key from the `ssh -G` command, it won't attempt to generate the keys. In many cases, this works. However, users should be able to specify that they only want to use codespaces generated keys (and effectively force the generation of the keys). 

Using these keys will make other SSH flows against codespaces easier because users will know that they can always get the right key. 

### Proposed solution

Add a flag to `gh cs ssh` that forces it to use `codespaces.auto` keys. 

The flag should probably be a boolean flag like `--codespaces-keypair` with a shorthand `-k`

review_comments: nit: I was thinking something like autoGenerateKeys etc.

That was actually what I started with :) 

The reason I changed was because the flag doesn't always cause the `ssh` command to _generate_ the key pair. It will use an existing pair if one exists. Users might think that providing this flag will always wipe out the existing keys to generate a new pair with the "generate" verbiage.
